The EPA filter is a cumulative measure of offensive efficiency, while the first-and-10 and no-huddle rates reflect tactical tendencies. Dualities emerge between EPA and tactical execution—high EPA may correlate with high first-and-10 success, but not always. The system assumes deterministic play classification and ignores dynamic variables like rush threat or receiver separation.
